jobs.title: Planning Officer (Career grade)
jobs.description:
* **Suffolk County Council**
* **Address:** Endeavour House, Ipswich, Suffolk IP1 2BX, hybrid working
* **Salary:** £26,016 - £40,444 per annum
* **Hours:** 37 hours per week, flexible working options available
* **Contract:** Permanent

We’re focused on making a meaningful difference to communities across Suffolk. How? By listening to our people learning from what they say and creating a culture of mutual respect, where everyone works together to achieve great things. As a **Planning Officer** in the **Development Management team** with **Suffolk County Council,** you’ll be as keen to collaborate and build a bright future as we are. So, to make a positive impact, connect with us and connect with a fantastic career.

**Reimagine the possibilities.**

**Your role and responsibilities**

As either a graduate or non-graduate, your work will make a significant input to the County Council’s planning team, including both forward planning and development management tasks. Our Career Pathway means you will be expected to work with more responsibility as you gain experience. There will be opportunities to work with different aspects of planning across the team. We will also support you with professional training, where needed.

The Career Pathway is designed around the Royal Town Planning Institute’s (RTPI) **Chartered Town Planner Apprenticeship,** which will advance your career to becoming Chartered Town Planner faster. You will keep a log of your experience, not only for the RTPI’s Assessment of Professional Competence, but also as evidence of progression to the next stage.

You will be part of a small but busy team consisting of town planners and other specialists, together with support staff. We are part of a wider group of professionals – transport planners; economic development officers; environmental specialists - working to support sustainable growth in Suffolk.

**You will need**

* the desire to see growth take place in a way which works with our environment and communities
* to seek to create solutions and be open to innovation
* ambition to continuously improve in everything you do, taking the initiative to learn and develop.

You'll study at London South Bank University so please click on the following link for their entry requirements - **Chartered Town Planner Apprenticeships | London South Bank University**

You can find more information in the Job and Person Profile (JPP), which you can find in the ‘How to apply’ section towards the bottom of this advert.

If you believe you can succeed in this role, apply. Even if you don't meet all requirements, still apply. We would appreciate the opportunity to consider your application.

**The team**

You will be part of a small but busy team consisting of town planners and other specialists, together with support staff. We are part of a wider group of professionals – transport planners; economic development officers; environmental specialists - working to support sustainable growth in Suffolk.

The Development Management Team is part of the Planning Team, with wider responsibilities around Planning Policy, Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects and Developer Contributions.

Our office days are usually on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Additionally, we practice hybrid working.

**Empowering Everyone**

We’re big believers in potential, possibility and the power of different ideas. We’re always searching for ways to encourage, respect and enable everyone to be the best they can be. We want to represent the diverse communities we serve. We welcome applications from all individuals, especially those from groups that are currently underrepresented in the organisation, as shown in our **Workforce Equality Report**.

**For more information**

Please contact **Andy Rutter** (Development Manager) for a casual conversation. You can reach them by emailing **andy.rutter@suffolk.gov.uk**.

**How to apply**

**Step 1 -** Read the **Job and Person Profile (Word)****.**

**Step 2 -** Click ‘Apply Now’ to start your online application.

**Step 3 -** Upload asupporting statementanswering the following questions below (no more than 400 words per question). You should use the **Supporting Statement template (Word)**.

1. Give an example of when you had to manage several competing tasks or deadlines. How did you prioritise your workload?

2. Give an example of when you had to learn a new process, system or area of knowledge quickly. What steps did you take to develop your understanding?

3. Planning often involves balancing different priorities and viewpoints. Tell us about a time when you had to consider differing opinions before reaching a conclusion or making a recommendation.

**Step 4 -** Upload a CV (without name and personal details).

**Please note:** Without a supporting statement and CV, your interest will not be progressed. Any supporting documents must be in either PDF or MS Word format.

For guidance on completing your application, please see our **How to Apply page**.

**Planning to use Artificial Intelligence (AI)?** Please ensure your application still reflects your own skills, experience and ideas. If used inappropriately, your application may not be processed. Please read our **guidance for using AI** to understand what’s acceptable.

**Do you need any reasonable adjustments to help you to apply?** If you are disabled and/or have additional support needs, you can request reasonable adjustments. You can do this by contacting our Recruitment Team at **recruitment@suffolk.gov.uk** or **03456 014412**. You can find examples of possible adjustments on our **Reasonable Adjustment pages**.

**Closing date:** 11.30pm, 20 October 2026.

**Interview date:** 4 November 2026.

This authority is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. DBS (Disclosure and Barring Service) checks or police vetting will be required for relevant posts. #

jobs.title: Graduate Planner
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Graduate Construction Planner to join our team based across London.

**Location:** Site & Office – London  
**Hours:** 40 hours per week  
**Starting Salary:** £31,000 per annum  
**Pathway:** Permanent, Full-time 2-year programme, leading to assistant level role upon completion with salary potential of CIRCA £38k  
**Starting date:** September 2027

**We are unable to offer certificates of sponsorship to any candidates in this role.**

  

As a Graduate Construction Planner, you will assist in developing, monitoring, and updating project schedules to ensure timely and efficient project delivery. This role is ideal for a recent graduate eager to begin a career in construction planning, offering hands-on experience, mentorship, and opportunities for professional growth. You'll work closely with the Senior Planner and project teams to create comprehensive schedules and keep projects on track.

**What will you be responsible for?**

As a Graduate Construction Planner, you'll be working within the planning team, supporting them in delivering projects on time and to the highest standards.

**Your day to day will include:**

* Assisting in creating and updating comprehensive project schedules, including timelines and resource allocations
* Coordinating with project teams and stakeholders to gather information and update project plans and progress records
* Utilising project management software to plan timeframes, record progress, and communicate outcomes
* Conducting site visits to gather data and verify progress against schedules
* Preparing progress reports, including critical path analysis, for project teams and senior management

**What are the benefits for you?**

* **Practical experience**: gain valuable hands-on experience in your field.
* **Skill improvement**: develop technical and professional skills.
* **Networking**:build professional relationships and expand your network.
* **Career insight**: gain insights into your chosen industry and potential career paths.

  

**What are we looking for?**

This role of Graduate Construction Planner is great for you if:

* Hold a degree in Construction Management, Construction Project Management, Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline
* Analytical thinking skills, strong communication and IT skills, exposure to Planning Software
* A genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction planning and the construction industry, with clear motivation to learn and develop professionally.
* Ability to prioritise multiple tasks and manage time effectively whilst maintaining high standards.
* Enthusiasm for learning new skills and knowledge, and the ability to adapt in response to feedback.
* Work effectively as part of a team, demonstrating collaboration, reliability, and respect for others.

**Rewards and benefits**

We're proud to be able to offer our brilliant people a wide variety of benefits that you can tailor to your needs. You can see more information of benefits here.

**Diversity and inclusion**

Making Kier a diverse and inclusive place to work is a huge priority for us. We're proud of the steps we've taken so far, but we know we must always do more. Our employees are key in shaping Kier's diversity and inclusion initiatives and our people have made a huge impact on how we work, by using their experiences to shape our policies. You can see our D&I action plan here.

As a Disability Confident employer, we will ensure that a fair and proportionate number of disabled applicants that meet the minimum criteria for this role will be offered an interview.

  

**Application Timeline**

October 2026: Initial applications

November 2026: Application reviews

January 2027: Virtual/in-person assessment centres

  

We look forward to seeing your application to #joinkier.

**It is important to note that in certain recruitment situations we reserve the right to close adverts early**

jobs.title: Development Management Officer
jobs.description:
* Salary range:

  £29,542 - £40,444
* Contract Type:

  Permanent
* Directorate:

  Place & Economy
* Closing Date:

  20 October 2026
* Pay Grade:

  7-9
* Weekly Hours:

  37

  

Start your career in planning with us - are you looking for your first role in planning?

Are you ready to take on the challenges and rewards of a career in planning and development? We're looking for a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join our Planning Service as a Development Management Officer.

Our Development Management Team plays a vital role in shaping the city and its surrounding countryside, assessing a wide range of development proposals—from local applications to major strategic schemes.

In this role, you'll be trained to manage a diverse caseload of planning and related applications, building valuable experience and developing your professional expertise. You'll also work alongside experienced Principal Planners, supporting the delivery of high-profile projects such as city centre developments and sustainable urban extensions.

We're committed to the growth and success of our officers. You'll benefit from structured internal training, opportunities to contribute to service improvement projects, and the potential to work towards professional accreditation with the Royal Town Planning Institute.

This is an excellent opportunity to build your career at a key early stage, within a supportive, collaborative team that is passionate about delivering high-quality planning outcomes.

If you're looking to make a real impact and grow your career in planning, we'd love to hear from you

**All about You**

Do you have a genuine interest for contributing to the future planning and delivery of economic growth and housing within a developing City environment? Are you committed to supporting a quality environment enabling access and opportunities for all?

We are looking for a individual who is willing to learn and adapt to changes, is able to work independently or as team and is motivated.

Have strong research and analysis skills, with ability to read and interpret legislation.

Having a Town Planning/Urban Planning or related degree is desirable, but above all we are looking for people with a strong interest in the built environment who want to improve the city of Peterborough.

**Our Benefits**
  
We value our colleagues and have developed a number of benefits in addition to our generous annual leave starting at 25 days + bank holidays, sick pay and local government pension scheme…

* Access to a range of benefits via our Employee Benefits Platform, including in-store and online discounts as well as our Cycle to Work and Home & Electronics schemes
* Buy up to 10 days additional annual leave (pro-rata)
* Access to car lease scheme
* Take your bank holidays flexibly to better suit your personal circumstances
* Make Additional Voluntary Contributions (Shared Cost AVCs) to your pension with tax and National Insurance savings
* Access to development opportunities including apprenticeships to support your personal and professional growth
* Paid volunteering hours each year so you can make a positive impact on our community during your normal working day
* Access to our equality, diversity and inclusion network
* Opportunities to receive Employee Recognition Awards
  

**Our Commitments**
  
We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer, dedicated to fostering diversity, advancing equity, and building an inclusive workplace for everyone. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourage those from underrepresented groups, including disabled people, care leavers, and individuals from minority ethnic communities. Your unique perspectives and experiences are encouraged and valued and will play a vital role in our success.
  
  
We are committed to making our recruitment process as accessible as possible. If you are a person who has or considers yourself to have a disability and you require reasonable adjustments to the application or interview process, please contact pccrecruitment@peterborough.gov.uk.
  
  
Appointment to this post will be subject to the outcome of an Enhanced Disclosure obtained through the Disclosure and Barring Service. The Council is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.

***If you've already applied and completed the recruitment process for this position within the last three months, there's no need to reapply. We really appreciate your interest and thank you for considering us.***

jobs.title: Graduate Planner
jobs.description:
**Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.**

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

**Who are we looking for?**

We're looking for a **Graduate Environmental Planner** to join our team! In this role, you will support environmental planning, permitting, impact assessment, regulatory compliance, and project delivery for environmental and infrastructure projects. You will work alongside multidisciplinary teams while building practical consulting skills through mentoring, structured learning, and varied project experience.

**Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.**

**Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:**

* Supporting environmental planning and environmental impact assessment projects through research, data collection, analysis, and reporting
* Assisting with environmental permitting and regulatory compliance activities, including materials needed for permits, approvals, and agency consents
* Researching land use planning, environmental regulations, public policy, and project development requirements
* Collecting, organizing, interpreting, and analyzing environmental, planning, and regulatory information to support project recommendations
* Preparing technical reports, permit applications, environmental documentation, meeting materials, and client deliverables
* Supporting project coordination, scheduling, document control, and other project management activities
* Assisting with proposals, bids, and tender responses by gathering and organizing required information
* Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and communicating with internal and external stakeholders
* Following applicable health, safety, and environmental policies and procedures
* Participating in technical training, professional development, and communities of practice

**What you will bring to the team:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, urban or regional planning, natural resources, sustainability, public policy, environmental studies, or a related field
* Strong interest in environmental planning, permitting, regulatory compliance, and impact assessment
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong research, analytical, and problem-solving abilities
* Ability to organize and interpret information from multiple sources and draw meaningful conclusions
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
* Ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize tasks, and meet commitments
* Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, accountability, and professionalism
* Ability to work effectively independently and as part of a collaborative team
* Internship, co-op, research, or academic project experience in environmental planning, permitting, environmental studies, or regulatory compliance preferred
* Familiarity with environmental assessment, GIS, data analysis tools, environmental research methods, or government approval processes is a plus

jobs.title: Assistant Planner
jobs.description:
**Our Story**

J.Crew gets you dressed every day, for every occasion.

Since 1983, we’ve been creating classics that feel familiar and refreshingly new, crafted with unbeatable quality and distinctive point of view—it’s no wonder we’ve been in your closet for four decades and counting.

Today, we continue to do the classics our way, inspiring not only how you shop but how you define your personal style. Our commitment runs deeper than just making great clothes—we’re proud of our role in getting you dressed with confidence, character, and celebrating a distinctly American sensibility that makes us who we are.

Our dedication to Diversity, Equity, Belonging & Sustainability has been celebrated with industry recognition, reflecting our commitment to fostering an inclusive and sustainable workplace.

**The Role + Purpose**

As an Assistant Planner, you’ll support your manager in developing and executing financial plans that balance sales, margin, and inventory goals. You’ll use data to understand performance, identify opportunities, and make recommendations that strengthen results. This role builds the foundation for a career in Planning — blending analytical curiosity, collaboration, and strategic thinking to bring product and financial strategies to life.

  
  

**Responsibilities:**

**Preseason**

* Support the creation of preseason sales, margin, and inventory plans by department, class, and style
* Analyze historical and current business trends to identify key learnings, risks, and growth opportunities
* Summarize key financial metrics — such as markup, margin rate, and average unit cost — to inform planning assumptions
* Partner with manager to align on seasonal investment strategy and product flow recommendations
* Collaborate with cross-functional partners to prepare financial presentations for line reviews and buy meetings

**In Season**

* Provide weekly and monthly business recaps that highlight performance trends and variances to forecast
* Update and reforecast sales, margin, and inventory plans based on current results and market shifts
* Partner with manager and cross-functional teams to identify in-season opportunities and risks, proposing actions such as receipt reflows, pricing adjustments, or markdowns
* Participate in OTB (Open-to-Buy) meetings and inventory reviews, ensuring alignment with departmental goals
* Maintain accuracy of all reports and tools to support effective, data-driven decision-making

**Qualifications:**

*Required:*

* 0–2 years of experience, recent college grad with internship experience or retail store experience preferred
* Strong analytical and financial skills, with proficiency in Excel and retail math
* Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation abilities
* Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
* Curious, proactive, and detail-oriented in a fast-paced environment
* Collaborative team player eager to learn and grow within Planning

*Preferred:*

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Merchandising, or a related field
* Exposure to planning, buying, allocation, or financial analysis within a retail or consumer goods organization
  

  

* This role follows our in-office work model, requiring associates to work from our New York office Tuesday through Thursday each week, effective September 8, 2026.

We welcome you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes. Our passion is scouting life-long learners who are driven by curiosity, and who feel connected to our brands and share our desire to make an impact. We’re always seeking bright new talent who leverage their unique experiences to discover, grow and evolve with our teams.

**Benefits + Perks**

* **Health & Well-being -** Eligible associates and family members receive medical, dental, prescription and vision insurance, family planning (fertility, adoption & surrogacy support), fitness discounts, medical travel and more.
* **Associate Discount -** We love our products just as much as you do! That’s why we offer a great associate discount across all of our brands (J.Crew, J.Crew Factory, and Madewell).
* **Summer Fridays -** In addition to our hybrid work model, we also close our office at 1:00 PM every Friday during the Summer months.
* **Community Impact -** We support the communities where we live and work through our philanthropic efforts and the J.Crew Cares Program.
* **Winter Break -** In addition to our PTO package, J.Crew Group offers a winter break at the end of December to eligible full-time associates at the Home Office to provide time to refresh and recharge.

Note: Availability of these benefits and perks may be subject to work location & employment type and may have certain eligibility requirements.

Hourly Range: $25.48 - $29.74

At J.Crew Group (JCG) we aim to pay competitively for our company’s size and industry. The base salary offered will take into account internal equity and may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region of work premises, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. The base salary is just one component of J.Crew Group’s competitive total rewards strategy that also includes the opportunity for bonus, competitive benefits and perks.

One of our core focuses here at JCG is creating a community and culture that builds belonging. We are deeply committed to our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion efforts, and we warmly welcome job applicants of all backgrounds.

  

JCG is proud to affirmatively provide equal opportunity to all associates and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin or citizenship, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, legally protected physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation or any other basis protected under applicable law.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Urban Planning and Hazards
jobs.description:
**The Department.** The Department of Earth, Environmental and Geographical Sciences (**https://geoearth.charlotte.edu/**) is a diverse community of physical, geospatial, and social scientists composed of over 36 faculty members, 398 undergraduate majors, and 86 graduate students. Our current mission is to inspire discovery of the Earth and its inhabitants and to foster informed communities of learners who strive for a sustainable world. We create and disseminate knowledge of the Earth’s human and natural systems to adapt to an ever-changing environment in which we live, work, and interact. The Department offers undergraduate degrees in Meteorology (BS), Earth and Environmental Sciences (BS), Geology (BS), Geography (BA/BS), and Environmental Studies (BA). At the graduate level, we offer an MS in Earth Sciences, an MA and PhD in Geography, and regularly participate in the interdisciplinary Infrastructure and Environmental Systems (INES) and Public Policy (PPOL) PhD programs and the Master’s in Urban Design (MUD). The Department is also home to the Center for Applied Geographic Information Science (CAGIS, **https://gis.charlotte.edu/**) and the Charlotte Action Research Project (CHARP, **https://charp.charlotte.edu/**). We are committed to excellence in disciplinary and interdisciplinary research and teaching.

  

**The College.** As the largest and most academically diverse college at UNC Charlotte, the College of Humanities & Earth and Social Sciences (**https://chess.charlotte.edu/**) houses 14 departments, 13 interdisciplinary programs, and 7 applied centers. We offer a wide range of undergraduate and graduate degree programs with extensive honors and early-entry options. The College plays a pivotal role in delivering on the university’s goals in the areas of research excellence, student success and experience, and community engagement. Through their scholarship and teaching, the College’s 350+ faculty members seek to deepen our understanding of complex problems and lead the university in interdisciplinary collaboration.

* **Suffolk County Council**
* **Address:** Endeavour House, Ipswich, Suffolk IP1 2BX, hybrid working
* **Salary:** £26,016 - £40,444 per annum
* **Hours:** 37 hours per week, flexible working options available
* **Contract:** Permanent

We’re focused on making a meaningful difference to communities across Suffolk. How? By listening to our people learning from what they say and creating a culture of mutual respect, where everyone works together to achieve great things. As a **Planning Officer** in the **Development Management team** with **Suffolk County Council,** you’ll be as keen to collaborate and build a bright future as we are. So, to make a positive impact, connect with us and connect with a fantastic career.

**Reimagine the possibilities.**

**Your role and responsibilities**

As either a graduate or non-graduate, your work will make a significant input to the County Council’s planning team, including both forward planning and development management tasks. Our Career Pathway means you will be expected to work with more responsibility as you gain experience. There will be opportunities to work with different aspects of planning across the team. We will also support you with professional training, where needed.

The Career Pathway is designed around the Royal Town Planning Institute’s (RTPI) **Chartered Town Planner Apprenticeship,** which will advance your career to becoming Chartered Town Planner faster. You will keep a log of your experience, not only for the RTPI’s Assessment of Professional Competence, but also as evidence of progression to the next stage.

You will be part of a small but busy team consisting of town planners and other specialists, together with support staff. We are part of a wider group of professionals – transport planners; economic development officers; environmental specialists - working to support sustainable growth in Suffolk.

**You will need**

* the desire to see growth take place in a way which works with our environment and communities
* to seek to create solutions and be open to innovation
* ambition to continuously improve in everything you do, taking the initiative to learn and develop.

You'll study at London South Bank University so please click on the following link for their entry requirements - **Chartered Town Planner Apprenticeships | London South Bank University**

You can find more information in the Job and Person Profile (JPP), which you can find in the ‘How to apply’ section towards the bottom of this advert.

If you believe you can succeed in this role, apply. Even if you don't meet all requirements, still apply. We would appreciate the opportunity to consider your application.

**The team**

You will be part of a small but busy team consisting of town planners and other specialists, together with support staff. We are part of a wider group of professionals – transport planners; economic development officers; environmental specialists - working to support sustainable growth in Suffolk.

The Development Management Team is part of the Planning Team, with wider responsibilities around Planning Policy, Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects and Developer Contributions.

Our office days are usually on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Additionally, we practice hybrid working.

**Empowering Everyone**

We’re big believers in potential, possibility and the power of different ideas. We’re always searching for ways to encourage, respect and enable everyone to be the best they can be. We want to represent the diverse communities we serve. We welcome applications from all individuals, especially those from groups that are currently underrepresented in the organisation, as shown in our **Workforce Equality Report**.

**For more information**

Please contact **Andy Rutter** (Development Manager) for a casual conversation. You can reach them by emailing **andy.rutter@suffolk.gov.uk**.

**How to apply**

**Step 1 -** Read the **Job and Person Profile (Word)****.**

**Step 2 -** Click ‘Apply Now’ to start your online application.

**Step 3 -** Upload asupporting statementanswering the following questions below (no more than 400 words per question). You should use the **Supporting Statement template (Word)**.

1. Give an example of when you had to manage several competing tasks or deadlines. How did you prioritise your workload?

2. Give an example of when you had to learn a new process, system or area of knowledge quickly. What steps did you take to develop your understanding?

3. Planning often involves balancing different priorities and viewpoints. Tell us about a time when you had to consider differing opinions before reaching a conclusion or making a recommendation.

**Step 4 -** Upload a CV (without name and personal details).

**Please note:** Without a supporting statement and CV, your interest will not be progressed. Any supporting documents must be in either PDF or MS Word format.

For guidance on completing your application, please see our **How to Apply page**.

**Planning to use Artificial Intelligence (AI)?** Please ensure your application still reflects your own skills, experience and ideas. If used inappropriately, your application may not be processed. Please read our **guidance for using AI** to understand what’s acceptable.

**Do you need any reasonable adjustments to help you to apply?** If you are disabled and/or have additional support needs, you can request reasonable adjustments. You can do this by contacting our Recruitment Team at **recruitment@suffolk.gov.uk** or **03456 014412**. You can find examples of possible adjustments on our **Reasonable Adjustment pages**.

**Closing date:** 11.30pm, 20 October 2026.

**Interview date:** 4 November 2026.

new_jobs.title: Graduate Planner
new_jobs.description:
We're looking for a Graduate Construction Planner to join our team based across London.

**Location:** Site & Office – London  
**Hours:** 40 hours per week  
**Starting Salary:** £31,000 per annum  
**Pathway:** Permanent, Full-time 2-year programme, leading to assistant level role upon completion with salary potential of CIRCA £38k  
**Starting date:** September 2027

**We are unable to offer certificates of sponsorship to any candidates in this role.**

  

As a Graduate Construction Planner, you will assist in developing, monitoring, and updating project schedules to ensure timely and efficient project delivery. This role is ideal for a recent graduate eager to begin a career in construction planning, offering hands-on experience, mentorship, and opportunities for professional growth. You'll work closely with the Senior Planner and project teams to create comprehensive schedules and keep projects on track.

**What will you be responsible for?**

As a Graduate Construction Planner, you'll be working within the planning team, supporting them in delivering projects on time and to the highest standards.

**Your day to day will include:**

* Assisting in creating and updating comprehensive project schedules, including timelines and resource allocations
* Coordinating with project teams and stakeholders to gather information and update project plans and progress records
* Utilising project management software to plan timeframes, record progress, and communicate outcomes
* Conducting site visits to gather data and verify progress against schedules
* Preparing progress reports, including critical path analysis, for project teams and senior management

**What are the benefits for you?**

* **Practical experience**: gain valuable hands-on experience in your field.
* **Skill improvement**: develop technical and professional skills.
* **Networking**:build professional relationships and expand your network.
* **Career insight**: gain insights into your chosen industry and potential career paths.

  

**What are we looking for?**

This role of Graduate Construction Planner is great for you if:

* Hold a degree in Construction Management, Construction Project Management, Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline
* Analytical thinking skills, strong communication and IT skills, exposure to Planning Software
* A genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction planning and the construction industry, with clear motivation to learn and develop professionally.
* Ability to prioritise multiple tasks and manage time effectively whilst maintaining high standards.
* Enthusiasm for learning new skills and knowledge, and the ability to adapt in response to feedback.
* Work effectively as part of a team, demonstrating collaboration, reliability, and respect for others.

**Rewards and benefits**

We're proud to be able to offer our brilliant people a wide variety of benefits that you can tailor to your needs. You can see more information of benefits here.

**Diversity and inclusion**

Making Kier a diverse and inclusive place to work is a huge priority for us. We're proud of the steps we've taken so far, but we know we must always do more. Our employees are key in shaping Kier's diversity and inclusion initiatives and our people have made a huge impact on how we work, by using their experiences to shape our policies. You can see our D&I action plan here.

As a Disability Confident employer, we will ensure that a fair and proportionate number of disabled applicants that meet the minimum criteria for this role will be offered an interview.

  

**Application Timeline**

October 2026: Initial applications

November 2026: Application reviews

January 2027: Virtual/in-person assessment centres

  

We look forward to seeing your application to #joinkier.

**It is important to note that in certain recruitment situations we reserve the right to close adverts early**

* Salary range:

  £29,542 - £40,444
* Contract Type:

  Permanent
* Directorate:

  Place & Economy
* Closing Date:

  20 October 2026
* Pay Grade:

  7-9
* Weekly Hours:

  37

  

Start your career in planning with us - are you looking for your first role in planning?

Are you ready to take on the challenges and rewards of a career in planning and development? We're looking for a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join our Planning Service as a Development Management Officer.

Our Development Management Team plays a vital role in shaping the city and its surrounding countryside, assessing a wide range of development proposals—from local applications to major strategic schemes.

In this role, you'll be trained to manage a diverse caseload of planning and related applications, building valuable experience and developing your professional expertise. You'll also work alongside experienced Principal Planners, supporting the delivery of high-profile projects such as city centre developments and sustainable urban extensions.

We're committed to the growth and success of our officers. You'll benefit from structured internal training, opportunities to contribute to service improvement projects, and the potential to work towards professional accreditation with the Royal Town Planning Institute.

This is an excellent opportunity to build your career at a key early stage, within a supportive, collaborative team that is passionate about delivering high-quality planning outcomes.

If you're looking to make a real impact and grow your career in planning, we'd love to hear from you

**All about You**

Do you have a genuine interest for contributing to the future planning and delivery of economic growth and housing within a developing City environment? Are you committed to supporting a quality environment enabling access and opportunities for all?

We are looking for a individual who is willing to learn and adapt to changes, is able to work independently or as team and is motivated.

Have strong research and analysis skills, with ability to read and interpret legislation.

Having a Town Planning/Urban Planning or related degree is desirable, but above all we are looking for people with a strong interest in the built environment who want to improve the city of Peterborough.

**Our Benefits**
  
We value our colleagues and have developed a number of benefits in addition to our generous annual leave starting at 25 days + bank holidays, sick pay and local government pension scheme…

* Access to a range of benefits via our Employee Benefits Platform, including in-store and online discounts as well as our Cycle to Work and Home & Electronics schemes
* Buy up to 10 days additional annual leave (pro-rata)
* Access to car lease scheme
* Take your bank holidays flexibly to better suit your personal circumstances
* Make Additional Voluntary Contributions (Shared Cost AVCs) to your pension with tax and National Insurance savings
* Access to development opportunities including apprenticeships to support your personal and professional growth
* Paid volunteering hours each year so you can make a positive impact on our community during your normal working day
* Access to our equality, diversity and inclusion network
* Opportunities to receive Employee Recognition Awards
  

**Our Commitments**
  
We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer, dedicated to fostering diversity, advancing equity, and building an inclusive workplace for everyone. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourage those from underrepresented groups, including disabled people, care leavers, and individuals from minority ethnic communities. Your unique perspectives and experiences are encouraged and valued and will play a vital role in our success.
  
  
We are committed to making our recruitment process as accessible as possible. If you are a person who has or considers yourself to have a disability and you require reasonable adjustments to the application or interview process, please contact pccrecruitment@peterborough.gov.uk.
  
  
Appointment to this post will be subject to the outcome of an Enhanced Disclosure obtained through the Disclosure and Barring Service. The Council is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.

***If you've already applied and completed the recruitment process for this position within the last three months, there's no need to reapply. We really appreciate your interest and thank you for considering us.***

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

**Who are we looking for?**

We're looking for a **Graduate Environmental Planner** to join our team! In this role, you will support environmental planning, permitting, impact assessment, regulatory compliance, and project delivery for environmental and infrastructure projects. You will work alongside multidisciplinary teams while building practical consulting skills through mentoring, structured learning, and varied project experience.

**Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.**

* Supporting environmental planning and environmental impact assessment projects through research, data collection, analysis, and reporting
* Assisting with environmental permitting and regulatory compliance activities, including materials needed for permits, approvals, and agency consents
* Researching land use planning, environmental regulations, public policy, and project development requirements
* Collecting, organizing, interpreting, and analyzing environmental, planning, and regulatory information to support project recommendations
* Preparing technical reports, permit applications, environmental documentation, meeting materials, and client deliverables
* Supporting project coordination, scheduling, document control, and other project management activities
* Assisting with proposals, bids, and tender responses by gathering and organizing required information
* Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and communicating with internal and external stakeholders
* Following applicable health, safety, and environmental policies and procedures
* Participating in technical training, professional development, and communities of practice

**What you will bring to the team:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, urban or regional planning, natural resources, sustainability, public policy, environmental studies, or a related field
* Strong interest in environmental planning, permitting, regulatory compliance, and impact assessment
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong research, analytical, and problem-solving abilities
* Ability to organize and interpret information from multiple sources and draw meaningful conclusions
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
* Ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize tasks, and meet commitments
* Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, accountability, and professionalism
* Ability to work effectively independently and as part of a collaborative team
* Internship, co-op, research, or academic project experience in environmental planning, permitting, environmental studies, or regulatory compliance preferred
* Familiarity with environmental assessment, GIS, data analysis tools, environmental research methods, or government approval processes is a plus

new_jobs.title: Assistant Planner
new_jobs.description:
**Our Story**

J.Crew gets you dressed every day, for every occasion.

Since 1983, we’ve been creating classics that feel familiar and refreshingly new, crafted with unbeatable quality and distinctive point of view—it’s no wonder we’ve been in your closet for four decades and counting.

Today, we continue to do the classics our way, inspiring not only how you shop but how you define your personal style. Our commitment runs deeper than just making great clothes—we’re proud of our role in getting you dressed with confidence, character, and celebrating a distinctly American sensibility that makes us who we are.

Our dedication to Diversity, Equity, Belonging & Sustainability has been celebrated with industry recognition, reflecting our commitment to fostering an inclusive and sustainable workplace.

**The Role + Purpose**

As an Assistant Planner, you’ll support your manager in developing and executing financial plans that balance sales, margin, and inventory goals. You’ll use data to understand performance, identify opportunities, and make recommendations that strengthen results. This role builds the foundation for a career in Planning — blending analytical curiosity, collaboration, and strategic thinking to bring product and financial strategies to life.

  
  

**Responsibilities:**

**Preseason**

* Support the creation of preseason sales, margin, and inventory plans by department, class, and style
* Analyze historical and current business trends to identify key learnings, risks, and growth opportunities
* Summarize key financial metrics — such as markup, margin rate, and average unit cost — to inform planning assumptions
* Partner with manager to align on seasonal investment strategy and product flow recommendations
* Collaborate with cross-functional partners to prepare financial presentations for line reviews and buy meetings

**In Season**

* Provide weekly and monthly business recaps that highlight performance trends and variances to forecast
* Update and reforecast sales, margin, and inventory plans based on current results and market shifts
* Partner with manager and cross-functional teams to identify in-season opportunities and risks, proposing actions such as receipt reflows, pricing adjustments, or markdowns
* Participate in OTB (Open-to-Buy) meetings and inventory reviews, ensuring alignment with departmental goals
* Maintain accuracy of all reports and tools to support effective, data-driven decision-making

**Qualifications:**

*Required:*

* 0–2 years of experience, recent college grad with internship experience or retail store experience preferred
* Strong analytical and financial skills, with proficiency in Excel and retail math
* Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation abilities
* Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
* Curious, proactive, and detail-oriented in a fast-paced environment
* Collaborative team player eager to learn and grow within Planning

*Preferred:*

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Merchandising, or a related field
* Exposure to planning, buying, allocation, or financial analysis within a retail or consumer goods organization
  

  

* This role follows our in-office work model, requiring associates to work from our New York office Tuesday through Thursday each week, effective September 8, 2026.

We welcome you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes. Our passion is scouting life-long learners who are driven by curiosity, and who feel connected to our brands and share our desire to make an impact. We’re always seeking bright new talent who leverage their unique experiences to discover, grow and evolve with our teams.

**Benefits + Perks**

* **Health & Well-being -** Eligible associates and family members receive medical, dental, prescription and vision insurance, family planning (fertility, adoption & surrogacy support), fitness discounts, medical travel and more.

**The Department.** The Department of Earth, Environmental and Geographical Sciences (**https://geoearth.charlotte.edu/**) is a diverse community of physical, geospatial, and social scientists composed of over 36 faculty members, 398 undergraduate majors, and 86 graduate students. Our current mission is to inspire discovery of the Earth and its inhabitants and to foster informed communities of learners who strive for a sustainable world. We create and disseminate knowledge of the Earth’s human and natural systems to adapt to an ever-changing environment in which we live, work, and interact. The Department offers undergraduate degrees in Meteorology (BS), Earth and Environmental Sciences (BS), Geology (BS), Geography (BA/BS), and Environmental Studies (BA). At the graduate level, we offer an MS in Earth Sciences, an MA and PhD in Geography, and regularly participate in the interdisciplinary Infrastructure and Environmental Systems (INES) and Public Policy (PPOL) PhD programs and the Master’s in Urban Design (MUD). The Department is also home to the Center for Applied Geographic Information Science (CAGIS, **https://gis.charlotte.edu/**) and the Charlotte Action Research Project (CHARP, **https://charp.charlotte.edu/**). We are committed to excellence in disciplinary and interdisciplinary research and teaching.

  

**The College.** As the largest and most academically diverse college at UNC Charlotte, the College of Humanities & Earth and Social Sciences (**https://chess.charlotte.edu/**) houses 14 departments, 13 interdisciplinary programs, and 7 applied centers. We offer a wide range of undergraduate and graduate degree programs with extensive honors and early-entry options. The College plays a pivotal role in delivering on the university’s goals in the areas of research excellence, student success and experience, and community engagement. Through their scholarship and teaching, the College’s 350+ faculty members seek to deepen our understanding of complex problems and lead the university in interdisciplinary collaboration.

  

**The University.** UNC Charlotte is an R-1 university, and the only research university in North Carolina’s largest metropolitan area. As the second-largest institution in the UNC System, we transform lives, communities, and industries through accessible and affordable education, offering exemplary bachelor’s, master’s, doctoral, and professional programs. Our commitment to scholarship, innovation, and service drives our contributions to the ever-evolving needs of society. Through strategic partnerships and a focus on real-world applications, we prepare our graduates to excel in their careers and lead with purpose and integrity in a rapidly changing world.

  

**Vacancy Open to**

All Candidates

  

**Description of Work**

The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.
  
Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.
  
Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.
  
Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.
  
  
This position is subject to research-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose, **either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application**, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.
